items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-11-10
items.q: They had Tony Papalia was with him down there.

ctx.x: I've heard him on records, huh?

Witt Lebowski. He had a brother who was a violinist. But Witt Lebowski had a way that he could break a string on a piano. Very easily. If he was mad at you, he'd close the piano down and put his feet up on the piano like this and wouldn't touch it. They had Tony Papalia was with him down there. Jimmy Boyle. Johnny Karugi was on fiddle. And the funny thing about it, Robert Morton and Ray McNamara were the organist. And I used to stay down there at night to close, to put, I don't know if I told you, to put the trap…

items.title: Godfrey Hirsch Interview, 1987-10-20
items.q: this guy dead. Paquet, the clarinet, there's Alessandro, there's Tony Papalia, Charlie Hartman...

ctx.x: Ed Fontana, any relation to Carl Fontana? No. No. No, no, no. Hector Fontana is his son. Ah, okay. Now, Leo Forbstein. That was his brother. His brother. Was he ever involved down here? No. Did he ever come here? No, no.

He was on the First National. He was at First National. But every one of these people, this is the only guy that I know if he's still alive. Every one of these guys are dead. So Alessandro, this guy dead. This guy dead. This guy dead. Paquet, the clarinet, there's Alessandro, there's Tony Papalia, Charlie Hartman, Fontana, Rico Condona, Johnny Detroit just died, Mike Apparello I know has been dead for quite a while, and Louis Primer's dead. Who goddamn band is dead? That's it that Blair sung Evolution of Music?…
